title: How does one product give six more?
description: From eighteen times twelve is two hundred and sixteen, six products with decimals are found by counting the digits after the point, the same way as the example in the book. The products below one are then picked out.
teaching_notes: One idea: the digits of the whole number product stay the same and only the place of the point changes, by the digits after the point in both numbers. Watch for students who move the point the wrong number of places or forget the zeros in front.

source: Given that 18 × 12 = 216, find the products: (a) 18 × 1.2 (b) 18 × 0.12 (c) 1.8 × 1.2 (d) 0.18 × 0.12 (e) 0.018 × 0.012 (f) 1.8 × 12. In which of the cases above is the product less than 1?
video_script.why: The child has seen that the digits after the point in a product are those of the two numbers added and now uses one known product for six decimal products.
video_script.substitution: the book's given product eighteen times twelve, and its six decimal products
video_script.anchor: Eighteen times twelve is two hundred and sixteen, and six decimal products to be found from it

final_answer.spoken: twenty one point six, two point one six, two point one six, zero point zero two one six, zero point zero zero zero two one six, and twenty one point six. The fourth and the fifth are less than one

maths_rules: a number below 1 times a number below 1 is below 1, in (d) and (e)
video_script.design: One idea: the digits two one six stay and the point moves by the digits after the point in both numbers. Assumes the digit rule. The six products stay all video; the decimals appear only on the answer beat.
